name: Critical Caste Studies: Culture, Society, and Thought
description: The objective of the course is to provide an in-depth study of caste and its critique in modern Indian thought. It invites us, first, to evaluate the textual links that bind the “enlightenment” and “Orientalist” discourse with the formation of collusive authority and national self-esteem. In relation, it calls to discuss and compare the “social vision” of anti-caste intellectuals in 19th and 20th century India. Second, it will introduce the academic trajectory of studies on caste and modern India, inviting us to understand the trajectory of thought against caste as an index towards a critical hermeneutics of history. The modules, lastly, would revolve around the writings of a series of thinkers who largely wrote on the themes and theories of caste, untouchability, religion, nation, and the world. The focus would be on four critics as writers: Jotirao Phule, Iyothee Thass, E. V. Ramasamy, and B. R Ambedkar; and these comparative figures would be evaluated for different themes in modern Indian culture, society and thought. Their works would be discussed for how they present a critique that (re)constructs the social constituency and community of their times, and how they offer a thematic reflection for our times. The course endeavours to engage with different concepts in their writings, relating them to an advancement of contemporary scholarship in the field.
